Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 50, "heading": "CHAPTER 48. DOMESTIC", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u050-b0062", "target": "Порой мне приходило на ум предположение: что могло бы случиться или что случилось бы, если бы мы с Дорой никогда не узнали друг друга? Но она так срослась с моим существованием, что это была пустейшая из всех фантазий, и вскоре она поднималась вне моей досягаемости и взора, как паутинка, плывущая в воздухе.", "source_sha256": "ca1fbef87c28756231150fa8b40fd3e3650fe26e27d3856388291640037b8c6b", "target_id": "ru-en85-u050-b0062", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "c185eab6307cbf0661ebe500a377999e7505e3bd2467831935af35aaa011f9e8"}, {"source_id": "en85-u050-b0063", "target": "Я всегда любил её. То, что я описываю, дремало, полупробуждалось и снова засыпало в сокровеннейших тайниках моего ума. Во мне не было тому никаких признаков; я не знаю, чтобы оно влияло на что-либо из того, что я говорил или делал. Я нёс бремя всех наших маленьких забот и всех моих замыслов; Дора держала перья; и мы оба чувствовали, что наши доли распределены так, как того требует дело. Она была искренне привязана ко мне и гордилась мной; и когда Агнес вписывала в письма к Доре несколько горячих слов о гордости и интересе, с какими мои старые друзья слышат о моей растущей известности и читают мою книгу, словно слышат, как я сам произношу её содержание, Дора читала их мне вслух, со слезами радости в ярких глазах, и говорила, что я милый, старый, умный, знаменитый мальчик.", "source_sha256": "f0378db851c2f5a88057aff75c6fab541db0052bff288cb678de89d3f3144bec", "target_id": "ru-en85-u050-b0063", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "0346fe5ea5ee27ae0817519cf426b4845d6cc1141620ce07a6de9d00d3a1417c"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 48, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u050-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The first mistaken impulse of an undisciplined heart.’ Those words of Mrs. Strong’s were constantly recurring to me, at this time; were almost always present to my mind. I awoke with them, often, in the night; I remember to have even read them, in dreams, inscribed upon the walls of houses. For I knew, now, that my own heart was undisciplined when it first loved Dora; and that if it had been disciplined, it never could have felt, when we were married, what it had felt in its secret experience.", "sha256": "eab51cad2c67775b78c64141d821efe7428c66ab0c4f5e715ca9fef982c48932", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘There can be no disparity in marriage, like unsuitability of mind and purpose.’ Those words I remembered too. I had endeavoured to adapt Dora to myself, and found it impracticable. It remained for me to adapt myself to Dora; to share with her what I could, and be happy; to bear on my own shoulders what I must, and be happy still. This was the discipline to which I tried to bring my heart, when I began to think. It made my second year much happier than my first; and, what was better still, made Dora’s life all sunshine.", "sha256": "16a19b223d9ab0d5a37a53882dc571b0afa7b9e91691bd2d87e0e1f049585144", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But, as that year wore on, Dora was not strong. I had hoped that lighter hands than mine would help to mould her character, and that a baby-smile upon her breast might change my child-wife to a woman. It was not to be. The spirit fluttered for a moment on the threshold of its little prison, and, unconscious of captivity, took wing.", "sha256": "87ca19ccc4a9244e341846ad78a62771b938bb15eb8f77e495c21f32a2894375", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘When I can run about again, as I used to do, aunt,’ said Dora, ‘I shall make Jip race. He is getting quite slow and lazy.’", "sha256": "2515b0bf4e9a73b69b9a222a5dd847ba4ea89ad2309ac5508c593b27de3fab89", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I suspect, my dear,’ said my aunt quietly working by her side, ‘he has a worse disorder than that. Age, Dora.’", "sha256": "86ad4f86b0b465204934b9440676e36b8f18914cffbc1654f705a7f2b8bf1387", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Do you think he is old?’ said Dora, astonished. ‘Oh, how strange it seems that Jip should be old!’", "sha256": "dc09d017ec4979fbfcb7c9a51f6c771ba40652fec1ce04ae0a86163e05d88ad0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s a complaint we are all liable to, Little One, as we get on in life,’ said my aunt, cheerfully; ‘I don’t feel more free from it than I used to be, I assure you.’", "sha256": "b5b4dd49a834e854832f2036237ed0bf70711ab2320a64ea6797efde4f8f27f3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘But Jip,’ said Dora, looking at him with compassion, ‘even little Jip! Oh, poor fellow!’", "sha256": "b6df767e2ca1e1fd23784f5c320967d823fdd76763935cc9fc1ab79d7c552c80", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I dare say he’ll last a long time yet, Blossom,’ said my aunt, patting Dora on the cheek, as she leaned out of her couch to look at Jip, who responded by standing on his hind legs, and baulking himself in various asthmatic attempts to scramble up by the head and shoulders. ‘He must have a piece of flannel in his house this winter, and I shouldn’t wonder if he came out quite fresh again, with the flowers in the spring. Bless the little dog!’ exclaimed my aunt, ‘if he had as many lives as a cat, and was on the point of losing ‘em all, he’d bark at me with his last breath, I believe!’", "sha256": "d53f7d30bd078d81dfd455edb54130eb6fd24559152ffb9220ddffe9feb677c6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora had helped him up on the sofa; where he really was defying my aunt to such a furious extent, that he couldn’t keep straight, but barked himself sideways. The more my aunt looked at him, the more he reproached her; for she had lately taken to spectacles, and for some inscrutable reason he considered the glasses personal.", "sha256": "6c2c682f8bc43fb7ebe0d8b439f61804af42fdada4bd018573cf2b39f3301e14", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora made him lie down by her, with a good deal of persuasion; and when he was quiet, drew one of his long ears through and through her hand, repeating thoughtfully, ‘Even little Jip! Oh, poor fellow!’", "sha256": "b1219fd071f03f3776ae2ce380877021e65c6ecb5d834b60913d2abcb1e145e4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘His lungs are good enough,’ said my aunt, gaily, ‘and his dislikes are not at all feeble. He has a good many years before him, no doubt. But if you want a dog to race with, Little Blossom, he has lived too well for that, and I’ll give you one.’", "sha256": "79036f6f6ec24c95cde3fa68634abbe752a083109b7bb82c77f1e00e6d278c69", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Thank you, aunt,’ said Dora, faintly. ‘But don’t, please!’", "sha256": "7402f6f66abbbbd488033abe27dc3f52d5633b1cfab38d9f6d4467d4c272934e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No?’ said my aunt, taking off her spectacles.", "sha256": "2518f4e6d0ba8465212bda551dae2946ad31c0f9bc69362b0eb56e5ab8f33a02", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I couldn’t have any other dog but Jip,’ said Dora. ‘It would be so unkind to Jip! Besides, I couldn’t be such friends with any other dog but Jip; because he wouldn’t have known me before I was married, and wouldn’t have barked at Doady when he first came to our house. I couldn’t care for any other dog but Jip, I am afraid, aunt.’", "sha256": "3fcaf08003217e53a00816557a018a66e1288aa82837156dc0a843c863761f54", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘To be sure!’ said my aunt, patting her cheek again. ‘You are right.’", "sha256": "db0d27562f8dca8a84aead0de1df03dbaddffb93fdcbc7e9d9ce14a43b4691a5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You are not offended,’ said Dora. ‘Are you?’", "sha256": "bdd5e50c0288c4fb00c723777228b6e255abf15ed382bf3d78e75e309b6817ba", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, what a sensitive pet it is!’ cried my aunt, bending over her affectionately. ‘To think that I could be offended!’", "sha256": "2193c2616192bcc6e27dcde36fbe9cc4a8899f07d41438322236aa932aec57d5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[81]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, no, I didn’t really think so,’ returned Dora; ‘but I am a little tired, and it made me silly for a moment—I am always a silly little thing, you know, but it made me more silly—to talk about Jip. He has known me in all that has happened to me, haven’t you, Jip? And I couldn’t bear to slight him, because he was a little altered—could I, Jip?’", "sha256": "23038d3a77a4c30721c387a483389980a92ad61386a36bcaed997f87038b6a32", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Jip nestled closer to his mistress, and lazily licked her hand.", "sha256": "f58cda992ae1223e4432da9030a3bf8368eff950443642784e6c6ea884358994", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You are not so old, Jip, are you, that you’ll leave your mistress yet?’ said Dora. ‘We may keep one another company a little longer!’", "sha256": "96253677a9820e3e7953e03b3a5e0e468b6e62d9d831529b3d0e06f7154bd5a5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My pretty Dora! When she came down to dinner on the ensuing Sunday, and was so glad to see old Traddles (who always dined with us on Sunday), we thought she would be ‘running about as she used to do’, in a few days. But they said, wait a few days more; and then, wait a few days more; and still she neither ran nor walked. She looked very pretty, and was very merry; but the little feet that used to be so nimble when they danced round Jip, were dull and motionless.", "sha256": "6c09949a92980023ad509a4891ff0e8514ac7d71b2ddd5f15a27899ee7c059aa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I began to carry her downstairs every morning, and upstairs every night. She would clasp me round the neck and laugh, the while, as if I did it for a wager. Jip would bark and caper round us, and go on before, and look back on the landing, breathing short, to see that we were coming. My aunt, the best and most cheerful of nurses, would trudge after us, a moving mass of shawls and pillows. Mr. Dick would not have relinquished his post of candle-bearer to anyone alive. Traddles would be often at the bottom of the staircase, looking on, and taking charge of sportive messages from Dora to the dearest girl in the world. We made quite a gay procession of it, and my child-wife was the gayest there.", "sha256": "ffe3a66ec0cf331d9dc4807bcbac26775bfdbe7997427ef4e0237b55723be984", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u050-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But, sometimes, when I took her up, and felt that she was lighter in my arms, a dead blank feeling came upon me, as if I were approaching to some frozen region yet unseen, that numbed my life. I avoided the recognition of this feeling by any name, or by any communing with myself; until one night, when it was very strong upon me, and my aunt had left her with a parting cry of ‘Good night, Little Blossom,’ I sat down at my desk alone, and tried to think, Oh what a fatal name it was, and how the blossom withered in its bloom upon the tree!", "sha256": "81b351ee8e36c93f8eefdd7f04670b9347f0e0be501124c4ea8e1d06eec4b46d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[55]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
